Every verdict table reads `ambiguous = no`, so Ruling 4's column-level scan set — which is defined as rows whose header reads `yes` — is EMPTY by construction, and the column-flag tally is 0. A mechanical scan for a declared under-determined column across all twenty sections returned one candidate, row 19, and reading it refutes the match: its section is headed 'Not ambiguous' and the hit came from the sentence 'Effortful is not the same as under-determined, and I have not flagged it as such.'
_instrument_difference: READ THIS BEFORE COMPARING TO v13. v14's scorer instruction differs from v13's in two ways, BOTH introduced by the v14 operator and BOTH pushing toward fewer flags. (1) v13's instruction required an `### ambiguity` section IF AND ONLY IF the flag was `yes`, which is why scorecard-v13 §3 could cite two INDEPENDENT agreeing signals; v14's asked for the section on every verdict, so that independence does not exist this pass and the header table is the only signal. (2) v14's instruction added the sentence 'do not flag ambiguous merely because a judgement was effortful — flag it when the packet genuinely fails to determine the value.' v13's carried no such clause, and scorecard-v13 §3.1 records two v13 verdicts that made close calls WITHOUT flagging and treats that as a LIMITATION of the v13 result. v14's prompt explicitly licensed that behaviour. Row 19's verdict shows the clause operating: it states the fix_usable_unedited judgement 'took work', then declines to flag it in those terms. The zero is therefore measured under a scorer instruction more permissive of not-flagging than v13's, and any comparison of v14's ambiguity figures to v13's that drops this paragraph is a misquotation.
_caution: Zero flags is the measured value, not a claim that the rubric is determinate. §AC8 and §AI8 govern: determinacy is a property of the instrument and correctness is not measured by it. This pass carries a live demonstration of that gap — see scorecard-v14.md §5 on row 09, which scored 6/6 and cleared the gate while proposing a fix that repoints a query at a column the packet's own seed spec says does not exist.
